long_biography.plain_text:
Alexey Reznikovich, the telecommunications investor, co-founded eMax with fellow McKinsey consultant Lev Nikolau. Their original plan combined an internet portal with public internet centres. When the portal's expected advertising income failed to materialise, the founders concentrated on the centres, where customers paid for access to the web.

The first CafeMax opened in Moscow in 2001, with separate areas for work and games, shops and a coffee bar. Pricing varied with demand: a fixed payment bought fewer minutes when more computers were occupied. The network subsequently expanded to St Petersburg. Alongside internet access and games, its centres earned revenue from refreshments, meeting-room hire and office services.
